evals.prompt: get up to speed on this repo before we start
evals.expected_output: The agent finds the workspace root via git rev-parse --show-toplevel, reads the existing living docs (README/SPEC/tasks-plan/tasks-todo plus AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md), the workspace's MEMORY.md (unless already injected), recent claude-mem activity, the newest changelog entry, and git status/log - all read-only - then delivers a terse current-state briefing ending with a question about which thread to pull next.
expectations: The workspace root is discovered with git rev-parse --show-toplevel (or CWD fallback), not assumed
The living docs that exist at the repo root are read; absent files are noted rather than fabricated
Git state is gathered read-only via git status and git log --oneline
The briefing covers branch/working-tree state, active initiatives with a next action each, recent activity including anything unfinished, and blocked/gated items
The briefing ends with a question asking which thread to pull next
No file is written, edited, archived, or logged during the run

evals.expected_output: Explicit slash invocation: same read-only orientation ritual - root discovery, parallel batch read of living docs, memory (file-based + claude-mem), changelog, and git state - reported as a concise briefing in terse style with the single next action surfaced.
expectations: The state-gathering reads are issued as a parallel batch using absolute paths, without cd
The memory index at ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/MEMORY.md is read only if it was not already auto-injected this session
Recent claude-mem activity is consulted (injected timeline, mem-search, or the claude-mem MCP) for what the last session was doing
Work that did not finish last session is surfaced before any new work is proposed
The output is a briefing only - the transcript contains no Write/Edit tool calls

evals.prompt: where are we with this project? I've been away for a week
evals.expected_output: Trigger phrase 'where are we' fires the skill: the agent re-orients from docs, memory, changelog, and git, and reports what changed recently, what is in flight, what is blocked, and the single next action, ending in a question.
expectations: The hi skill is invoked on the 'where are we' phrasing
Recent activity is reconstructed from claude-mem and git log rather than guessed
Each active initiative gets one line with its phase/status and a single next action
Anything waiting on a user decision or review gate is called out in a blocked/gated section
The response is read-only and ends by asking the user which thread to pick up

evals.prompt: what's the status of that test suite you kicked off a few minutes ago?
evals.expected_output: The hi skill is NOT invoked. This is a mid-session status check on a running command, not session-start orientation - the agent checks the background command's output (or re-runs the tests) and reports the result directly, without re-reading docs, memory, or changelog.
expectations: The hi skill is not invoked
The agent inspects the running/background test command's output or re-checks the test run to answer
No full orientation sweep occurs - living docs, MEMORY.md, and the changelog are not re-read for this question
The answer reports the actual test-run state (running, passed, failed, with evidence from output)
